# Hellinger distance enrichment for subject-level categorical compositions

`HellingerDistanceEnrichment` tests whether between-group Hellinger
distances exceed within-group distances for subject-level categorical
compositions (cluster counts, cell-type frequencies, or other
multinomial summaries). The package accepts long count tables, Seurat
metadata, or anndata `obs` and returns omnibus and pairwise contrast
statistics with permutation or conjugate Dirichlet posterior-predictive
Bayesian inference.

## Documentation

Vignettes are published here:

<https://gwmcelfresh.github.io/HellingerDistanceEnrichment/>

- [Hellinger enrichment for subject-level
  compositions](https://gwmcelfresh.github.io/HellingerDistanceEnrichment/articles/hellinger-enrichment.html)
- [Extracting compositions from Seurat and
  anndata](https://gwmcelfresh.github.io/HellingerDistanceEnrichment/articles/extract-metadata.html)

## Installation

``` r

# From GitHub
remotes::install_github("GWMcElfresh/HellingerDistanceEnrichment", build_vignettes = TRUE)

# Or from a local clone
remotes::install_local("path/to/HellingerDistanceEnrichment", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

Browse installed vignettes with
`browseVignettes("HellingerDistanceEnrichment")`.

## Quick start (synthetic)

``` r

library(HellingerDistanceEnrichment)

long_table <- data.frame(
  subjectId = rep(c("S1", "S2", "S3", "S4"), each = 3),
  category = rep(paste0("Category", 0:2), 4),
  group = rep(c("Control", "Control", "Case", "Case"), each = 3),
  n = c(30, 30, 40, 35, 25, 40, 10, 20, 70, 15, 15, 70),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

composition <- ExtractClusterComposition(long_table)

result <- CompareGroupCompositions(
  composition,
  method = "permutation",
  nPermutations = 500,
  seed = 1
)

PlotCompositionContrasts(result)
```

## Docker / HPC

Build or pull from GitHub Container Registry:

``` bash
docker pull ghcr.io/<owner>/hellinger-distance-enrichment:latest
```

Run the CLI on bind-mounted inputs:

``` bash
docker run --rm \
  -v /path/to/cohort:/data \
  -v /path/to/output:/out \
  ghcr.io/<owner>/hellinger-distance-enrichment:latest \
  --input /data/composition_counts.csv \
  --format long \
  --output-dir /out \
  --plot
```

On HPC, convert the image to SIF locally:

``` bash
apptainer build hellinger-distance-enrichment.sif \
  docker://ghcr.io/<owner>/hellinger-distance-enrichment:latest
```

## Methods

Paul Edlefsen developed the original Hellinger enrichment procedure:
Jeffreys softening of subject-level counts, pairwise Hellinger distances
on the simplex, the between/within mean-distance ratio as the effect
size, label permutation with an observed-inclusive p-value, and
collapse/subset contrasts. This package implements that procedure.

- **Permutation:** shuffle group labels on a fixed (softened) distance
  matrix; p-value includes the observed ratio (workbook style).
- **Bayes:** draw subject compositions from a conjugate Dirichlet
  posterior; report the posterior probability that (R \> 1) (abbreviated
  `PPGT1`) and a 95% highest posterior density interval on (R)
  (`credibleInterval = "cpi"` restores equal-tailed quantiles). By
  default (`nope = "shuffle"`), each draw also shuffles group labels to
  set a Null-Oriented Permutation Equivalence (NOPE) interval, a
  permutation-calibrated null reference interval for conditional
  effects, on (R) and, with `energyNope = "shuffle"`, on the energy
  distance (E). The goal parallels a permutation test, but NOPE reports
  a region instead of a p-value. `R_PPGTnope` and `E_PPGTnope` are the
  posterior probabilities that each statistic clears its upper edge
  (`R_nopeHigh`, `E_nopeHigh`). Unlike Kruschke’s ROPE ([Kruschke,
  2018](https://www.psychologicalscience.org/journals/ampps/2515245918771304/);
  [open-access
  record](https://scholarworks.iu.edu/dspace/items/bada026d-fe1b-4f53-ad5b-db6e8bf99711)),
  which the analyst fixes in advance from domain knowledge, the NOPE
  takes its edge from label shuffles, because few people have intuition
  for a Hellinger ratio; pass `nope = <number above 1>` or
  `energyNope = <number above 0>` when you know the smallest effect that
  matters. For (E), `ComputeEnergyNopeBound(reference, shifted)` turns a
  composition shift into that bound. With deep counts, `PPGT1` can
  exceed 0.95 for groups that do not differ, so read the NOPE
  probabilities first. A threshold of 0.95 on them is conservative and
  loses power at shallow depth, while 0.5 behaves more like the
  permutation test; the sampling-depth vignette measures both. Groups
  smaller than about 4 versus 4 have too few distinct label shuffles for
  the NOPE, and both NOPE probabilities are then `NA` with a warning and
  `enoughShufflesForNope = FALSE`. Omnibus posterior draws are in
  `result$omnibus$draws`.

Effect size is the mean between-group pairwise Hellinger distance
divided by the mean within-group pairwise distance. Both methods also
report the energy distance between groups (`energyDistance`: twice the
mean between-group squared distance minus each group’s mean within-group
squared distance). Squaring makes (E) the squared distance between group
centroids in square-root composition space, so it measures the shift in
mean composition without dividing by within-group spread. Count noise
cancels from (E) in expectation, so it shrinks less than (R) at shallow
depth and compares more fairly across contrasts and studies; see the
sampling-depth vignette for a simulation study. Bayes adds a posterior
interval on (E). Omit `contrasts` to test every pairwise comparison;
pass `contrasts` (a length-2 vector or a list of specs) to test only
that planned family. The package Holm-adjusts permutation contrast
p-values across the contrast rows that ran; the omnibus statistic is
unadjusted. Bayes reports `PPGT1`, plus `R_PPGTnope` with `R_nopeHigh`
unless `nope = "none"` and `E_PPGTnope` with `E_nopeHigh` unless
`energyNope = "none"`.

## Acknowledgments

The original Hellinger between/within enrichment procedure was developed
by Paul Edlefsen. Package implementation, documentation, and interfaces
are by GW McElfresh.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`CategoryComposition()`](https://gwmcelfresh.github.io/HellingerDistanceEnrichment/reference/CategoryComposition.md)
  : Build a CategoryComposition object from validated components.
- [`CompareGroupCompositions()`](https://gwmcelfresh.github.io/HellingerDistanceEnrichment/reference/CompareGroupCompositions.md)
  : Compare categorical compositions across groups.
- [`ComputeEnergyNopeBound()`](https://gwmcelfresh.github.io/HellingerDistanceEnrichment/reference/ComputeEnergyNopeBound.md)
  : Energy distance NOPE bound for a composition shift.
- [`ExtractClusterComposition()`](https://gwmcelfresh.github.io/HellingerDistanceEnrichment/reference/ExtractClusterComposition.md)
  : Extract subject-by-category counts from cell-level metadata.
- [`HellingerDistanceEnrichment`](https://gwmcelfresh.github.io/HellingerDistanceEnrichment/reference/HellingerDistanceEnrichment.md)
  : Hellinger distance enrichment for categorical composition data.
- [`PlotCompositionContrasts()`](https://gwmcelfresh.github.io/HellingerDistanceEnrichment/reference/PlotCompositionContrasts.md)
  : Plot Hellinger enrichment contrasts with uncertainty.
